answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through a ridge of escalating, non-refundable work bonds: each new agent must finish verifiable micro-tasks whose cost rises with every identity it controls, so spawning a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousandfold the work. Peers audit completed tasks at random; a failed audit burns the bond and sends an echo of the failure across the reputation graph, poisoning the whole cluster. Honest agents climb out of the dune of probation fast, while sybils drown in their own replication cost.
